newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER UNCONCERNED BY FIFA DEADLINE ON RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER UNCONCERNED BY FIFA DEADLINE ON RONALDO.

text.p: Internazionale on Tuesday heralded the imminent arrival of Ronaldo and said they were unconcerned by a FIFA ruling which orders them to agree a transfer fee with Barcelona for the Brazilian striker by the end of the month.
"Now Ronaldo is really ours. The operation is concluded," a triumphant Inter president Massimo Moratti told reporters.

Moratti acknowledged Inter still had to agree a transfer fee for the world footballer of the year and said he saw no reason, as things stood, for Inter to pay any more for him than the $26.3 million they had agreed to pay Barcelona to buy the player out of his contract.
"FIFA has allowed the transfer to go ahead and that is very important," Moratti said.
"Barcelona continue to say the $26.3 million is a penalty fee, to which another sum should be added to account for the value of the player.
"Instead, from the contract it is clear that the $26.3 million is all that we need to spend for Ronaldo."
But Moratti said he did not rule out the possibility of reaching a deal with Barcelona without FIFA intervention.
He said if an agreement was not forthcoming by July 31 -- the deadline FIFA has set for an accord to be reached -- Inter would be happy for soccer's world governing body to act as abitrator.
"If the demands are unjust we will arive at July 31 and FIFA will decide. If they are just there are many ways to reach an agreement," he said.
FIFA cleared the way for Ronaldo to join Inter when it said earlier on Tuesday the 20-year-old was free of any contractual obligations with Barcelona.
FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said Ronaldo had legitimately bought out his employment contract with the Spanish club for four billion pesetas ($26.3 million).
He noted, however, that this payment was not related to any additional transfer fee and said FIFA wanted the two European soccer giants to agree on such a fee by July 31.
"If no agreement is reached by that date FIFA will impose a fee which shall be binding," Blatter said.
Ronaldo's agent, quoted from Brazil by Italian media, said the player would arrive in Italy on Friday, and Moratti said he could be playing in Inter's famous black and blue stripes within days.
"As soon as next Sunday we will be able to see him in action against Manchester United," said Moratti, whose side play the English champions in a friendly in Milan.
